report_name: FBI Investigates Massive Leak of 170M+ North American ID Scans

threat_actors.name: Nexus Operator
threat_actors.description: The operator of the 'Nexus' dark web marketplace, responsible for selling a database containing over 170 million digital identity document scans from North American citizens. The operator advertised the service on the Russian-language cybercrime forum 'Exploit'.
threat_actors.goals: Financial profit from the sale of stolen personal identity documents.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor likely exploited a public-facing application, such as an API endpoint of a third-party identity verification service, to gain initial access to the backend infrastructure.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Information Repositories
attack_patterns.description: After gaining access, the threat actor accessed and exfiltrated a database of over 170 million ID scans from a compromised information repository, likely belonging to an identity verification provider.

identities.name: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
identities.description: The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation, which has launched an investigation into the 'Nexus' dark web service and the associated data breach.

identities.name: IDScan.net
identities.description: A third-party identity verification provider mentioned in reporting as a primary focus of the investigation, though its involvement as the source of the breach is unconfirmed.

identities.name: Brian Krebs
identities.description: A journalist whose own driver's license was used as a free sample by the 'Nexus' site operator on a cybercrime forum to prove the authenticity of the stolen data.

infrastructure.name: Nexus Marketplace
infrastructure.description: A dark web marketplace offering a searchable database of over 170 million stolen identity document scans for sale.

infrastructure.name: Exploit Forum
infrastructure.description: A notorious Russian-language cybercrime forum where the operator of the 'Nexus' marketplace advertised the data leak service to the criminal underground.

indicators.name: Potential Identity Verification API Abuse
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Identity Verification API Abuse
id: 9c5b1a3d-4e8c-4f7b-8d1a-9e2b3c4d5e6f
status: experimental
description: Detects traffic to a common identity verification API endpoint pattern. This activity is not inherently malicious but should be monitored for unusually high volumes of data egress, which could indicate a breach similar to the 'Nexus' marketplace incident.
references:
  - https://www.kompas.id/artikel/fbi-investigates-leak-of-millions-of-us-citizens-data
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-03
tags:
  - attack.t1213
  - attack.collection
level: low
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/api/v1/verify_id'
      - '/api/verify'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: This behavioral indicator detects access to common API endpoints used for identity verification, based on hunting hints provided in the report. It is intended to flag activity that should be monitored for high volume or anomalous data egress.
